subject: Dedicated capacity – session-shape & token-topology survey
messages:
From: Alex Yu <alex@vectralabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vectralabs.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake — quick overview request

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this. We are moving toward a reserved/dedicated deployment for our primary inference stack and want to get a sensible sizing baseline before the executive review next month. High level: customer-facing chat agent (multi-turn), some async batch embedding jobs, and a small reranking pipeline.

Can you share the specific telemetry and shape questions you need so we can pull the right logs from our staging cluster? We can attach a small sample export. Ideal goals: p50 token latency under 120ms, p95 under 350ms; cost predictability is important.

Also looping in Procurement for contracting timeline.

Appreciate a focused checklist we can answer in-line.

— Alex
Alex Yu
Head of Platform Engineering, Vectra Labs
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Alex Yu <alex@vectralabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@vectralabs.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — quick overview request

Hi Alex — thanks, and congrats on getting this staged. Below is a concise survey that will let us size a dedicated fleet and recommend autoscaling/burst guardrails. If you can paste short answers or attach the sample CSV you mentioned, we can produce a preliminary capacity sketch within 48 hours. I attached a small sample CSV schema (sample_telemetry.csv) you can use.

Priority: please answer items 1–6 first; 7–12 are helpful for tuning.

1) Workload breakdown (percent of requests by surface): chat-generation, system batches (embeddings), rerank. Provide percentages that sum to 100.
2) Session vs stateless: are chats session-affine (KV cache kept per user session)? If so, typical session duration and average tokens per session (including prompts and model responses).
3) Prompt/response token distributions: give a token distribution or simple buckets (e.g., 60% prompts <128 tokens, 30% 128-512, 10% >512) and average response length per bucket.
4) Concurrency profile: typical sustained concurrent sessions, expected daily peak concurrency, and the 99th percentile burst (for example sustained 200, peak 1,200, p99 burst 2,500).
5) Request rate shape: percent of traffic that is streaming vs non-streaming; percent of requests that are short polling (sub-second) vs long-poll (multi-second).
6) Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 token-level or response-level targets, and whether you require strict hard SLOs or best-effort.
7) KV cache & reuse: do you have high prefix reuse that benefits KV caching? Typical shared prefix reuse percentage across sessions.
8) Batch/offline jobs: number of embedding batches per day, average tokens per job, and preferred scheduling windows (e.g., overnight).
9) Model variants: which model families/size do you intend to serve in Dedicated (e.g., 13B quantized, 70B int8); if mixing, what percent of requests go to each?
10) Safety/QA: do you require synchronous moderation or pre/post-filtering that adds extra token passes per request?
11) Availability/region: preferred region(s), any cross-region failover requirements, and maintenance windows.
12) Telemetry sample: attach 72 hours of representative telemetry (timestamps, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, model, session_id). CSV or parquet is fine.

Attachments included: sample_telemetry.csv (schema), vectra_data_schema.png (for reference).

If any of the items above are unknown, approximate numbers are fine — we'll flag assumptions in the estimate. Shall we schedule a 30-minute sizing review after you return the answers?

Thanks,

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
From: Alex Yu <alex@vectralabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vectralabs.com>
Date: 2029-04-17T11:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — quick overview request

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the checklist. Answers below; I attached a 72-hour sample export (attached as sample_telemetry.csv). Let me know if any item needs deeper detail.

1) Workload breakdown: chat-generation 72%, embeddings/batches 18%, rerank 10%.
2) Session vs stateless: Chat is session-affine. Typical session duration: 7 minutes. Average tokens per session: prompts 220 tokens, model responses 450 tokens (average); so ~670 tokens/session total.
3) Token distribution: prompts: 55% <128, 30% 128-512, 15% >512. Responses: 50% <128, 35% 128-512, 15% >1024.
4) Concurrency profile: sustained concurrency 240, daily peak 1,600, p99 instantaneous burst we observed at 2,900. We expect some smoothing after autoscaling but need headroom for marketing spikes.
5) Streaming vs non-streaming: 65% streaming, 35% non-streaming. 80% of requests are short-interaction (sub-second backend compute), 20% are multi-turn generator churn causing longer tails.
6) Latency SLOs: target p50 response under 100ms, p95 under 300ms, p99 under 600ms. Hard SLO for p95 is important for UX; p99 we accept occasional soft deviations.
7) KV cache reuse: moderate — shared prefix reuse ~18%. We have user-specific context wedges that benefit from warm KV caches.
8) Batch jobs: ~12 embedding batches/day, average 300k tokens per job, run in two windows (0100-0400 and 1400-1500).
9) Model variants: primary production 13B quantized (approx 80% of traffic), fallback 33B int8 (20%) for higher-quality responses.
10) Safety/QA: synchronous moderation applied to ~20% of outputs (adds approx +4 token passes on average).
11) Availability/region: single-region (us-west) preferred with cold-standby in us-east for DR. Maintenance windows negotiable nights/weekends.
12) Telemetry sample: attached. File includes columns: timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, session_id, request_id, route_id.

Let us know if you want a small zoom to walk through the CSV. Procurement is fine with an initial sketch; they asked for the rough monthly committed GPU estimate for budgeting.

— Alex
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Yu <alex@vectralabs.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@vectralabs.com>
Date: 2029-04-18T16:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — quick overview request

Looping in Marissa for commercial alignment and adding a quick first-pass sizing note based on the numbers Alex provided. This is a conservative sketch — we will refine after stepping through the CSV and confirming sequence length tails.

Preliminary notes (assumptions flagged):
- Primary model: 13B quantized, 80% of calls. Fallback 33B int8, 20%.
- Sustained concurrent sessions: 240. Peak concurrency planning: 1,600 sustained day peak, p99 instantaneous 2,900.
- Average tokens/session ~670. Average tokens per second per session is variable due to streaming; we assume average emission velocity of 40 tokens/sec when streaming.

Capacity sketch (round numbers):
- Baseline reserved fleet: 12 x A40-class GPUs (quantized optimized) with headroom for session affinity and KV cache. This assumes 13B quantized at ~2.8x concurrency per GPU for sustained low-latency workloads.
- Burst pool: additional 6-8 GPUs in a burst tier (on same dedicated pool) or autoscale into on-demand to cover p99 spikes to 2,900 concurrency.
- Embedding batch windows: schedule next to off-peak (0100-0400) with task draining and prewarming; 1-2 GPUs dedicated to batch during windows or use spot where allowed.

Estimated committed monthly GPU ask for budgeting: 12 reserved GPUs, 8 capacity for burst (mix reserved+on-demand) => recommend starting commit at 12 with a 6–9 month review to avoid over-commit. Commercial terms to follow; Marissa, can you prepare a draft monthly commitment quote and a burst addon?

Clarifying questions for Alex (quick):
1) Can you confirm the CSV includes a per-request flag for streaming? If not, we can infer from latency shapes but prefer explicit.
2) For the 13B quantized workload, do you have an experimental concurrency-per-GPU estimate from your staging runs? That will help tighten the baseline.
3) Do you have a guaranteed DR failover RTO? If less than 15 minutes we should plan cross-region warm standby.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute sizing review tomorrow where I’ll walk through the CSV and show how we map token shapes to GPU throughput and KV cache efficiency.

Thanks —
--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
